about.title: Personal Injury Help in Sonoma, California
about.longDescription: Sonoma is a small town with busy stretches — Broadway, 5th Street W, W Napa Street, and Rt 12 see a steady flow of local and visiting traffic, and public records show 41 injury collisions in the most recent final year, leaving 51 people hurt. Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to show up more often in these reports, likely tied to end-of-week traffic and weekend visitors heading into wine country. Getting hurt in a collision or other accident here can leave you dealing with medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls you didn't ask for. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people in Sonoma with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at your situation and explain your options. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers money for you. We don't practice law or handle your case ourselves; we simply help you find someone who can. If you've been injured, reaching out costs nothing and can help you understand where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why People in Sonoma Turn to LawProactive

items.title: You Have a Limited Window
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the chance to recover anything.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you share some blame for what happened, you can still recover compensation reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so your compensation isn't artificially capped.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover Money
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning you pay nothing upfront and owe no fee unless they win compensation on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Sonoma?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If a government entity is involved, the window can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation early.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partly to blame. Your total recovery would simply be reduced by your share of fault.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service that helps injured people in Sonoma find an independent personal injury attorney. We don't provide legal representation ourselves.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Sonoma?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along Broadway, 5th Street W, W Napa Street, and Rt 12, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. appearing more often in reports. These are simply neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything upfront to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is free, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
